kai-sre: Quick broadcast: running a short rollback-drill tonight 23:00-23:15 UTC to validate our automated SLO rollback path. Scope: internal canaries only.

nora-prodeng: Remind me the rollback trigger?

kai-sre: If p99 > 2x baseline for 10m or route.error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, system should auto-trigger SLO-rollback policy which pins routes to previous stable model and pauses canary traffic. We want to verify the automation and oncall handoffs.

aj-platform: I'll create a temporary metric tag `drill=slo-rollback-200555` and set autoscaler to conservative for the window.

sam-oncall: I'll be primary. Runbook: 1) Watch serving.p99, route.error_rate, rollback.trigger_count 2) If automation fails, run manual revert: `redwoodctl rollout revert --route <canary> --to stable`; then notify customers if >30m. 3) If controlplane alerts present, escalate.

sre-ops-bot: Scheduled job "slo-rollback-drill-2005551111" -> Tue 2005551111T23:05:00Z.

kai-sre: Test plan: induce synthetic latency on canary for 12m starting at 23:05, expect automation to detect and perform rollback within 5m after thresholds hit.

aj-platform: Prechecks done: kvcache hitrate 94%, all replicas healthy.

sre-ops-bot: Synthetic latency injection started (23:05 UTC).

sam-oncall: Seeing p99 spike to ~2.3x baseline. rollback.trigger_count incremented.

kai-sre: Automation performed rollback at 23:09: verified route pinned to stable model and canary traffic paused.

sam-oncall: No unexpected node restarts, no customer routes impacted.

aj-platform: Post-run quick metrics: rollback latency from trigger ~120s, serving.p99 returned to baseline within 90s after rollback. Minimal cost impact.

nora-prodeng: This validates the automation. I'll update the SLO playbook with observed detection windows and update the alert thresholds to match.

kai-sre: Thanks team. Closing the drill. Full writeup and graphs in #eng-sre/postmortems later today.
